items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: However, I was playing with Thad Jones and Gil Evans and Joe Henderson and Kenny Dorham, and Clark Terry before I joined that band.

ctx.x: My father was in show business, and my mother was a violinist in Vaudeville. My father was a dancer and a comedian. And my whole family had a great sense of humor, and what’s left of it has. And I always loved the humor that Dizzy had in his playing, Clark [Terry] has a lot of humor in his playing, and to me humor and warmth kind of go together in a way. Louis Armstrong, his playing was real serious, but he would lighten it up with his conversation and his —

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was just going to say Lew Soloff. Let’s see. Who else was in there? ... We had Victor Sproles on bass. Don Friedman was there for a while

ctx.x: I was just going to say Lew Soloff. Let’s see. Who else was in there? A little cat that ended up in the Basie band. He was my manager’s son, Carley – Dale Carley, a great little player. We had Victor Sproles on bass. Don Friedman was there for a while, and – I can see these cats. I can’t call all their names right now.
Did Ron Carter play in that band?
